item.title: Understanding Decoding in Reading Development
item.description:
Decoding is a foundational reading skill where students recognize letter sounds and blend them together to translate written words into speech. The process involves recognizing letters and patterns (like b, sh, igh), knowing their sounds, and blending them to read words (e.g., /c/ - /a/ - /t/ becomes "cat").

Reading Rockets offers research-based decoding activities organized by grade level: - Kindergarten: Phonics and decoding activities - First Grade: Phonics and decoding activities - Second Grade: Phonics and decoding activities - Third Grade: A video demonstration showing how 3rd graders use syllables to decode longer words

item.title: Health Reminder About Flu and Illness
item.description:
The school is experiencing an increase in flu and seasonal illnesses. Keep your child home if they have: fever (100°F+), vomiting/diarrhea, significant cough, sore throat with fever, body aches, extreme fatigue, or flu-like symptoms. Students must be fever-free for 24 hours without medication and symptom-free for 24 hours after vomiting/diarrhea before returning to school.

item.title: Reading Corner's January Newsletter on Fluency
item.description:
The Reading Corner has published their January newsletter focusing on reading fluency. Fluency is the ability to read accurately, at an appropriate pace, and with expression. Families can help students increase fluency through regular reading and rereading of familiar books, practicing sight words in context, reading aloud with expression, and discussing stories. A helpful resource is Reading Rockets, which offers family-friendly tips and videos. Contact Reading Corner instructors for questions: Mrs. Geshan at geshanc@talawanda.org, Mrs. Kobermann at kobermanc@talawanda.org, or Mrs. Walters at waltersh@talawanda.org.
